narration.description: Spoken consequence of the mutations the tracker will have applied. Pure prose: no state, no rules text, and no number the tracker did not produce. Say it before the mutations, because it is voiced while they are still being generated.

mutations.description: Applied by the deterministic tracker as soon as this array closes, BEFORE any of the narration is voiced. Every entry must be valid or the whole round is rejected.

id.description: stable id within this round, e.g. m1

tool.description: Name one of the 7 tools the tracker implements, exactly. These are ALL of them: craft_item, take_item, drop_item, transfer_item, move_to, award_xp, introduce_npc. There is no damage, spend, give, craft, heal, attack or move tool - a roll is theatre, harm is a narration the gate never sees, and XP is award_xp. An unknown name rejects the whole round.

actor.description: The party slot performing THIS mutation, 1-4. It must be the slot that issued the intent named in `intent`, and that is the single most common way a round gets rejected: take_item, drop_item and transfer_item are all performed by a player, so their actor is that player's slot, never null and never somebody else's. null means the world acted (introduce_npc, award_xp with party:true).

intent.description: The id of ONE entry from the intent table in the prompt, e.g. i1. Copy it; prose in this field is not authority and a mutation whose actor has no matching intent is rejected NO_INTENT.

args.description: Arguments for this tool only. craft_item: name, item_type (weapon|armour|tool|consumable), materials [{name,qty}] from the ACTOR's own materials. take_item: item. drop_item: item. transfer_item: item, to_slot (the giver is the actor, not an argument). move_to: location. award_xp: amount with either slot 1-4 or party true. introduce_npc: name, role, portrait true. Anything the rules do not name is rejected with the allowed values attached.

description: Emission order: narration BEFORE mutations, so TTS can start while the mutations are still being generated. The gate applies nothing until the whole object parses, so this buys 3.1-6.8s of spoken latency and costs nothing (notes/voice-stack.md). Key order is the order of `properties`, not of `required` - the grammar walks properties. Never add a non-property key to `properties` (a `_note` key there becomes a field the model must emit).
